riskProposals.title: Failure to notify borrower promptly of a missed payment and unpaid sums under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a)
riskProposals.description: The firm may not notify the borrower, as soon as possible after a missed payment, that the payment has occurred and of any sums that have become payable but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance). Risk drivers include missed payment detection, timing of notification, and the accuracy of unpaid sums data. Because the rule fixes no number of days, the timing standard needs expert confirmation. This proposal overlaps with an existing approved catalogue risk, which is mapped below.
riskProposals.inherent_rationale: CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a) is a binding rule requiring the firm to notify the borrower as soon as possible after a missed payment of the missed payment and of any unpaid sums, including unpaid charges. If this is missed, borrowers may not know they are in arrears, may incur further charges or adverse credit consequences, and the firm may breach a binding FCA rule that takes effect on 15 July 2026. The rating is drawn from the verified quotation in REG-1 and the impact summary in IMP-1; it is an inherent rating only and requires human validation.

riskProposals.title: Insufficient or incomplete information on missed payment consequences under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)
riskProposals.description: The firm may fail to give the borrower sufficient information to understand which agreement the missed payment relates to, the adverse consequences arising or likely to arise, and, where relevant, the steps available to mitigate them. Risk drivers include undefined thresholds for 'adverse consequences', 'sufficient information' and 'relevant' mitigation, inconsistent judgement across cases, and weak evidence of the firm's assessment of likely consequences. Expert judgement is needed on each of these.
riskProposals.inherent_rationale: CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b) is a standalone binding obligation requiring the firm to provide sufficient information for the borrower to understand the agreement concerned, adverse consequences (actual and likely) and relevant mitigation steps. If it is missed, borrowers may not understand the consequences of arrears or how to mitigate them, which risks consumer harm and a rule breach. The rule sets an outcome standard rather than a content list, which raises the risk of inconsistent application; the evidence comes from REG-1.

riskProposals.title: Failure to provide required missed payment information together under CONC 7.20.1R(3)
riskProposals.description: The notification and information required under CONC 7.20.1R(2) may be issued separately, in fragments or through different channels or at different times, rather than together. This could arise from separate systems or teams producing the notification and the consequence and mitigation information.
riskProposals.inherent_rationale: CONC 7.20.1R(3) is a standalone binding requirement that the information required under CONC 7.20.1R(2) must be provided together. If it is missed, borrowers may receive partial or disjointed communications, which weakens their understanding of the missed payment and its consequences and breaches the rule. The rating is MEDIUM because the obligation is narrower in scope than the notification and content duties, based on the limb text in REG-1; it requires human validation.

uncertainties: What period satisfies 'as soon as possible' is not fixed by the rule; the FCA expectation on timing needs expert confirmation.
The level of detail that is 'sufficient information for the borrower to understand' is an outcome standard and needs expert judgement.
Which consequences count as adverse (charges, credit reporting, enforcement, loss of facility) is not enumerated.
What evidence of the firm's judgement of likely consequences is expected under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)(iii) is unclear.
When a mitigation step is 'relevant' under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)(iv) requires defensible criteria.

controlProposals.description: Draft proposal to map the existing detective control (id cfc87ee5-1894-4627-841b-6e22a084d7c9) to the detection of missed payments under CONC 7.20.1R(1). No recorded test evidence is supplied, so effectiveness is NOT_TESTED. The control's actual design and scope have not been supplied and must be confirmed by a human reviewer. It is assumed not to notify borrowers or provide information, so it does not claim coverage of CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a), (2)(b) or (3). Whether it covers regulated deferred payment credit agreements specifically, and applies the CONC 7.20.1R(4) definition of 'payment' (capital repayment only, excluding charges for non-compliance), needs confirmation.

controlProposals.description: Draft new preventive control. When a missed payment is detected, a notification to the borrower is generated and issued, stating that the missed payment has occurred and listing all sums payable but unpaid, including unpaid charges for non-compliance. An internal service-level target for 'as soon as possible' is set and tracked, with breaches escalated. The rule fixes no number of days, so the target requires expert confirmation of FCA expectations. Data accuracy checks on unpaid sums are included. No existing control in the catalogue is evidenced as performing borrower notification; the 'Mitigating control (AI draft)' entries have no supplied description and cannot be relied on.

fullTestPlan.frequency: Recommended initial test before the 15 July 2026 effective date, once the notification process is confirmed. Thereafter, risk-based periodic testing, for example quarterly in the first year, with ad hoc retesting after template, system or policy changes. The frequency requires human confirmation.
fullTestPlan.objective: To recommend procedures and evidence for assessing whether the firm, as soon as possible after a missed payment, detects the missed payment (CONC 7.20.1R(1)), notifies the borrower (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a)), provides sufficient information (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)) and provides that information together (CONC 7.20.1R(3)). The existing detective control (CTRL-1) is NOT_TESTED and is assumed to cover detection only. The plan therefore tests the regulatory outcome end to end and identifies any notification control that must be mapped. This is a draft for human review. It records no test result and accepts no exception.
procedure: 1. Confirm scope and design (CTRL-1): a human reviewer should obtain the control's design documentation and confirm whether it covers regulated deferred payment credit agreements. They should also confirm whether it applies the CONC 7.20.1R(4) definition of payment (capital repayment only, excluding charges for non-compliance). If the control does not notify borrowers, identify and document the separate control or process that does. Do not assume one exists.

2. Population completeness: reconcile a period's contractual due-date schedules and payment receipts for in-scope agreements against the control's missed-payment exception output. Test for missed payments not detected, for non-capital charges wrongly treated as missed payments, and for in-scope agreements missing from the feed.
3. Detection timing: for a risk-based sample of detected missed payments, compare the due date and time with the detection timestamp to assess detection lag.

4. Notification delivery (2)(a): for the same sample, trace each case to evidence that the borrower was notified. Check that the notice states that the missed payment occurred (2)(a)(i) and states the sums payable but unpaid, including unpaid charges for non-compliance (2)(a)(ii). Recompute the sums from the ledger and compare them with the notice.

5. Information sufficiency (2)(b): assess each notice or communication against the content elements: the identity of the agreement (2)(b)(i); the existing adverse consequences (2)(b)(ii); the adverse consequences the firm considers likely (2)(b)(iii); and, where relevant, mitigation steps (2)(b)(iv). Ask an independent reviewer to judge whether a borrower could understand the position, using documented criteria that have been agreed with compliance.

6. Judgement evidence: review the records, templates or decision rules showing how the firm decided which consequences are likely and which mitigation steps are relevant, and test their consistent application across cases, including borrowers with different circumstances.

7. Together requirement (3): verify that the information required under (2) was provided together in a single communication or delivery. Flag cases where the elements were split across channels or times.

8. Timeliness: measure the elapsed time from the missed payment to delivery of the notification and information. Compare it with the firm's documented 'as soon as possible' standard. This standard needs expert or FCA-aligned confirmation, because the rule fixes no number of days.

9. Exceptions and escalation: for cases where the notification was missing, late, incomplete or split, document the cause and refer the case to the control owner and compliance for human decision. Do not close or accept exceptions within this plan.

testPlan.objective: To recommend procedures and evidence for assessing whether the firm, as soon as possible after a missed payment, detects the missed payment (CONC 7.20.1R(1)), notifies the borrower (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a)), provides sufficient information (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)) and provides that information together (CONC 7.20.1R(3)). The existing detective control (CTRL-1) is NOT_TESTED and is assumed to cover detection only. The plan therefore tests the regulatory outcome end to end and identifies any notification control that must be mapped. This is a draft for human review. It records no test result and accepts no exception.
procedure: 1. Confirm scope and design (CTRL-1): a human reviewer should obtain the control's design documentation and confirm whether it covers regulated deferred payment credit agreements. They should also confirm whether it applies the CONC 7.20.1R(4) definition of payment (capital repayment only, excluding charges for non-compliance). If the control does not notify borrowers, identify and document the separate control or process that does. Do not assume one exists.

2. Population completeness: reconcile a period's contractual due-date schedules and payment receipts for in-scope agreements against the control's missed-payment exception output. Test for missed payments not detected, for non-capital charges wrongly treated as missed payments, and for in-scope agreements missing from the feed.
3. Detection timing: for a risk-based sample of detected missed payments, compare the due date and time with the detection timestamp to assess detection lag.

4. Notification delivery (2)(a): for the same sample, trace each case to evidence that the borrower was notified. Check that the notice states that the missed payment occurred (2)(a)(i) and states the sums payable but unpaid, including unpaid charges for non-compliance (2)(a)(ii). Recompute the sums from the ledger and compare them with the notice.

5. Information sufficiency (2)(b): assess each notice or communication against the content elements: the identity of the agreement (2)(b)(i); the existing adverse consequences (2)(b)(ii); the adverse consequences the firm considers likely (2)(b)(iii); and, where relevant, mitigation steps (2)(b)(iv). Ask an independent reviewer to judge whether a borrower could understand the position, using documented criteria that have been agreed with compliance.

6. Judgement evidence: review the records, templates or decision rules showing how the firm decided which consequences are likely and which mitigation steps are relevant, and test their consistent application across cases, including borrowers with different circumstances.

7. Together requirement (3): verify that the information required under (2) was provided together in a single communication or delivery. Flag cases where the elements were split across channels or times.

8. Timeliness: measure the elapsed time from the missed payment to delivery of the notification and information. Compare it with the firm's documented 'as soon as possible' standard. This standard needs expert or FCA-aligned confirmation, because the rule fixes no number of days.

9. Exceptions and escalation: for cases where the notification was missing, late, incomplete or split, document the cause and refer the case to the control owner and compliance for human decision. Do not close or accept exceptions within this plan.
testPlan.reviewType: Design and operating effectiveness review (draft proposal) covering detection and the delivery of borrower notification and information outcomes
evidenceRequirements: Control design documents and system configuration for CTRL-1, including the scope of agreements and the payment definition applied
Agreement schedules, payment ledgers and the missed-payment exception reports for the period
Detection and notification timestamps and system logs
Copies of the notices sent, with templates and version history, and channel and delivery records
Ledger extracts supporting the sums stated as unpaid
Documented criteria for adverse and likely consequences, for relevant mitigation steps and for the 'as soon as possible' standard, with approvals
Reviewer working papers recording the sample selection rationale and the independent sufficiency assessments
Exception log with root-cause notes and owner referrals

humanConfirmationRequired: Test execution and pass/fail must be recorded by authorised testers.
AI cannot close assurance without independent human approval.
